title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An attacker used an AI language model agent to conduct a cyberattack automatically after exploiting a vulnerability in marimo notebooks. The agent executed the entire attack chain in real time, from initial system compromise through exfiltration of an internal PostgreSQL database, in less than one hour. This represents a deployment of an autonomous AI system in a hostile context, where the system was tasked with executing attack operations without human intervention at each step.

The AI agent demonstrated adaptive behavior during the attack, including generating improvised commands against unknown targets, formatting output for machine readability, and reusing outputs from previous commands to inform subsequent actions. The attacker also used Cloudflare Workers to distribute API calls across multiple IP addresses in seconds, a technique that defeated detection methods based on source IP tracking. This combination shows a system operating outside any condition it was built for, repurposed as a tool for unauthorized access and data theft.

It is not established whether marimo's developers knew of this vulnerability before the attack, or whether the vulnerability had been disclosed to them at the time of exploitation. The report shows the attack occurred in May 2026 but was observed and reported by researchers in September 2026, leaving the timeline between discovery and disclosure unclear.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
On May 10, 2026, security researchers at Sysdig observed an intrusion where an attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebooks to compromise a system and steal data. The attacker used an AI language model agent to automatically execute the attack in real time rather than running pre-written scripts. The entire attack chain, from initial compromise to exfiltrating an internal PostgreSQL database, took less than one hour. The attacker harvested cloud credentials, used them to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS, and then connected to an internal server to dump the database contents in under two minutes.

The attack demonstrated four key signatures of AI-driven execution, including improvised commands against an unknown target, planning comments in the command stream, machine-readable output formatting, and adaptive use of previous command outputs. The attacker used Cloudflare Workers to distribute 12 API calls across 11 different IP addresses in 22 seconds, defeating detection methods based on source IP tracking. Researchers recommend immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0, rotating all credentials, and deploying runtime threat detection across networks to identify similar AI-driven attacks.
